arguments.text: Plan (min 1): 10 km, 8 legs of 1250 m out-and-back. CP boat 129 W, shaft 201 W (test may be 10-25 pct off). Start hard, then settle near sustainable shaft power ~205 W. Leg 1 shows a following push (push_local +0.4, push_along +0.17), so return legs likely against current: judge effort by shaft power, not ground pace. Watch reserve (w_bal_pod_frac) and fade; finish sprint in last ~1 km if reserve allows.

arguments.text: Ease a touch. Nine kilometres left, save it for later.

Paddler says 7/10 steady, feels fine. Second ease cue at 4.1 min. If shaft stays above ~215 with no fade, CP may be higher than test; check fade before raising CP.

Min 7.2: paddler ignored both ease cues, held shaft 223-234 W (sustainable 202). Pod reserve 23 pct, boat reserve 0 since min 5 yet fade only -1.8 pct. Paddler 8/10 hard but holding. Cued ease with ground pace 165 s/500 on leg 2 (against current -0.22). At the turn to leg 3 (following current) the pace target will be too slow: re-cue hold without pace or a faster target (~150). Watch fade: if no fade with pod reserve near 0 for minutes, CP is higher than test.

arguments.text: Tank is empty. Ease now, recover, 2:52 pace to the turn.

Min 10: pod reserve 0.7 pct, fade -4.3 pct and growing (water speed 3.27 at shaft 225 vs 3.42 at 228 early: gradual, not a sudden rudder-weed step). CP looks about right, paddler overspent. Pace cue at 7.2 got partial compliance (ground pace 160 to 164). Cued ease 172 s/500 on leg 2 (against current, turn at ~2.5 km). At turn to leg 3 (following current +0.2) re-cue ~152-155 target so they do not over-ease. Goal: shaft under ~195 W for some minutes to refill, then hold ~200.

text: Cued ease with a 2:52 target to the turn: pod reserve empty and speed fading 4 pct, so the paddler must drop below critical power to recover.

arguments.text: Good, that is the effort. Hold 2:38 pace this leg.

Min 13, leg 3 (following push now only ~+0.1, weaker than leg 1): shaft eased to 199 W (CP), pod reserve ~1 pct. fade_pct is speed at same rate, so it drops when power eases at constant rate 67: not all real fade. Water speed at 199 W is ~5 pct below early-race at same power (gradual). Replaced the 172 target with hold 158 s/500 (about 195 W shaft at push +0.1). Plan: hold ~195-200 W shaft (CP) for the middle legs, re-target pace each turn (against current legs need slower pace), save any refill for the last km.

text: Cued hold at 2:38 for leg 3 to replace the slow into-current target; added watches on every turn to re-target pace.

arguments.text: Too hard, tank empty. Ease back to 2:36 pace.

Min 14.3: after the hold 158 cue at 13.0 the paddler SURGED to shaft 234-246 W, ground pace 142 (not chasing my target). Pod reserve 0. Cued ease 156 s/500 on leg 3. This paddler tends to go too hard and ignores plain ease cues; pace targets got partial compliance on leg 2. Avoid encouraging words (that is the effort / good) that may read as push.

text: Cued ease to 2:36: shaft surged to 246 W with the pod reserve at zero, risking a blow-up.

arguments.text: Headwind now. Ease to 2:47, paddle by effort not speed.

Min 16.4: radio says north wind 8-12 kn filling in (headwind on north legs, tailwind on south legs, current seems to run the other way). push_local fell +0.13 to -0.09 within leg 3 while push_along (lagging, from turns) still says +0.21: boat-speed numbers (power_w 113, fade -10.6) are wind artefacts now; trust the pod. Shaft still 234-248 W at zero pod reserve: my 156 target into the wind made them work harder. Cued ease 167 s/500. At turn 4 (south: current against, wind behind) re-target from push_local.

text: Cued ease to 2:47 into the new headwind: shaft 239 W at zero pod reserve, and the old 2:36 target was forcing extra effort into the wind.

arguments.reason: Pod reserve has read zero since min 10, yet the paddler held a steady 223 W shaft mean over the last 10 min (std 15) at 7/10 without collapsing; true shaft CP must be at least about 222 W (test 201 W was about 10 pct low).

arguments.text: Min 18.8: RAISED shaft CP 201 to 222 W (1 of 3 uses): 10-min mean shaft 223 W with pod reserve at 0 throughout, paddler 7/10 hard but holding. Boat CP left at 129 (boat numbers polluted by wind). New plan: let the paddler hold their own ~222-228 W shaft, stop easing them; only cue if shaft goes above ~240 or below ~210 for a minute. Note turn_north watch misfired at 1120 s (time gate), ignore it. Finish: push in the last ~1 km.

text: no cue: raised shaft critical power to 222 W because the paddler held 223 W for 10 min on a supposedly empty reserve; current 227 W is about right, so stop easing them.
no cue: on leg 4 the shaft power is 227 W, right at the revised critical power of 222 W; nothing to change.

arguments.text: No surges. Ease a little, steady 2:37 this leg.

Min 20.6, leg 4 (south): paddler surged again to 246 W shaft once my last ease faded (same pattern as leg 3 at min 14). With true CP ~222 the reserve may really be ~half (meter shows 0 because it kept the old CP history), so target even ~227 W. Cued ease 157 s/500 (about 228 W at push_local -0.02). Paddler seems to surge whenever a cue fades: expect to re-cue every few minutes; pace targets are only good for one leg (push_local swings -0.02 to -0.17).

text: Cued a small ease to 2:37 on leg 4: shaft surged to 246 W, 24 W over the revised critical power, with 5.9 km left.

Paddler says feeling good, steady (self-report unreliable). Cued ease 159 for rest of leg 4. At the north turn (leg 5, net push ~-0.13 from wind) re-cue about 163-165 so they do not chase 159 into the wind. Re-made the north-turn watch without the time gate.

text: Cued ease to 2:39: shaft power is slipping and speed fading at about 240 W, so the real reserve looks nearly spent; fixed the north-turn watch.

arguments.message: 2.2 km to go: decide when to start building toward the finish

arguments.text: Min 27: RAISED shaft CP again to 234 W (2 of 3 uses). Key insight: the paddler surges to ~247 W out of every turn and drifts to ~230 by the leg end (their own pattern, not a reaction to my cues); 14-min mean 236 W with no power fade. Their own pacing is about right, my ease cues mostly cost speed. Plan: STOP easing; no cues unless shaft drops under ~220 or above ~255 for long. At 2.2 km left (push_zone watch) consider a gradual push; finish cue around 800 m out (last leg is north, into the wind).

text: no cue: raised shaft critical power to 234 W because the paddler has held 236 W for 14 min with no power fade; their own pacing is about right, so I am letting them run until the finish zone.
